solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Small dishes of baked pasta

indicators.note: something baked has been cooked and transformed, so the following word's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A menu description of little plates of oven-baked pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are the Spanish bar snacks served as a spread of small plates.

clue.text: Try out some concrete structures

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run sitting across them

parts.note: the run straddles the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An engineer trialling a few concrete buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: To test something is to trial it to see whether it works, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Last bit is removed from aircraft design

indicators.note: the final letter is taken off the word that follows

explanation.surface: An engineer trimming the tail off an aeroplane's blueprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a design or scheme drawn up in advance, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Fuddy-duddy leaving to prepare for a fight

parts.note: a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person
to be off is to be leaving

explanation.surface: An old fogey departing so as to get ready for a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To square off is to take up a fighting stance facing an opponent, an idiom.

clue.text: More masculine merchant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: comparative of butch, meaning manly
second meaning: a trader who sells meat

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a burlier trader; the first reading splits the word as a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Butch means manly so its comparative fits the first; a meat seller is a kind of tradesman for the second.

clue.text: Cereal with extremely dry liquor

parts.note: bran is the husk of cereal grain

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the outermost letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Breakfast cereal served alongside a very dry spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, an example of a liquor.

clue.text: Bath however is upside down

indicators.note: in a down entry, being turned upside down means the letters read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A bathtub that has been flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' looks like the city in Somerset, but it is the vessel you wash in.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is a bath, the vessel you sit in to wash.

clue.text: Scottish celebration to monopolise mother? On the contrary!

parts.note: to hog is to keep all of something for yourself
ma is a familiar word for mother
nay is an old word of contradiction, rather, no

explanation.surface: Someone accused of keeping mother to themselves at New Year protests the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary!' looks like a reversal signal, but it simply supplies a word of contradiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year's Eve festivity, the definition naming its national character.

clue.text: Leftover lira used carelessly

indicators.note: carelessly means without order, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Some spare Italian currency spent without thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' does double duty: its letters are fodder and, with 'carelessly', it reads as the signal; the lira was Italy's currency before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Residual describes what remains after the rest has gone, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Kitchen implement alas put in a stew

indicators.note: being in a stew means in a state of agitation, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A cook lamenting that a utensil has been dropped into the stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is a flat-bladed tool used for turning and spreading in cooking.

clue.text: Fake swamp near America

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A fake marshland supposedly close to America.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means counterfeit or not genuine, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Dim seabird flying around wedding participant

indicators.note: something flying around moves every which way, so the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A stupid gull circling over a wedding guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid attends the bride at a wedding, so she is one of its participants.

clue.text: Astronaut's gear made from second rate diamonds, say

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second
diamonds is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Astronaut kit cheaply made from inferior gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second rate' reads as one adjective meaning poor, but the words split into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacesuit is the pressurised outfit an astronaut wears outside a craft.

clue.text: Stars kind to plug Sinatra classic?

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so one word is pushed into the middle of another

parts.note: My Way is the famous song Frank Sinatra recorded

explanation.surface: Promoting a Sinatra standard, with stars kindly helping.
explanation.walkthrough: ILK goes after the M of MY WAY. 'Stars' looks like celebrities, but it is the galaxy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Milky Way is our galaxy, the band of countless stars across the night sky.

clue.text: Uproar when wearing gaudy jewellery that's very bright

indicators.note: something worn is wrapped round its wearer, signalling one piece set inside another

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A noisy fuss over flashy jewellery that dazzles.
explanation.walkthrough: Bling is slang for showy jewellery; here the jewellery does the wearing, wrapped round the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Blinding light is so bright it dazzles the eyes, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Arctic homes initially interest grand ladies and gents

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
the Ladies and the Gents are public toilets, which are loos

explanation.surface: Arctic housing at first attracting genteel men and women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies and gents' looks like people, but in Britain the Ladies and Gents are the signs on public toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: Igloos are dome-shaped snow shelters built by Inuit people, homes of the Arctic.

clue.text: Crazy to discard small piece of fruit

indicators.note: discarding means throwing away, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: It would be mad to throw out a little fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana is a single long yellow fruit, a piece of fruit.

clue.text: Clumsily enacts mountaineering objective

indicators.note: doing something clumsily means messing it up, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: An awkward performance of a climb to a summit.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb to the top, the aim of any mountaineering trip.

clue.text: Flier featuring chess piece and chess player, we hear?

parts.note: the king is the key chess piece

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Bobby Fischer was the American world chess champion

explanation.surface: A plane or pilot sporting chess motifs and a grandmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingfisher is a small brightly coloured bird, and a bird is a flier.

clue.text: Revolutionary starts to make another red xylophone

indicators.note: starts points to the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Instructions to build a second red percussion instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl Marx was the political thinker behind revolutionary communism, an example of a revolutionary.

clue.text: Place where officers eat pickle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a military dining hall
second meaning: a muddle or predicament

explanation.walkthrough: 'pickle' suggests a condiment on the officers' table, but it means a sorry plight.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is the forces' dining room, and also a jam or tricky situation, as is a pickle.

clue.text: Complain and drink, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word is matched on its sound

explanation.surface: Someone moaning and drinking, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: To whine is to grumble in a petulant voice, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bird stuck in the mud

indicators.note: stuck in means lodged inside, so the letters sit within the next words

explanation.surface: A large bird bogged down in the mire.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Teach Europeans to hide old gold coin

indicators.note: hiding something means concealing it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: E for European, twice for the plural
a ducat was a gold coin used across medieval Europe

explanation.surface: Telling Europeans to conceal an antique gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural Europeans gives two Es, one either side.
explanation.definitionFit: To educate is to teach or instruct, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Dairy product initially of great help in tent

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the following word

parts.note: a yurt is a round Central Asian tent

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: Yoghurt praised as a great help on a camping trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' covers all three of the words after it, not just the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoghurt is fermented milk, one of the foods made from dairy.

clue.text: Sat around hugging old partner in US state

indicators.note: hugging means holding something close inside the arms, so one piece wraps another
turned around means facing the other way, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: Someone sitting cuddled up to a former lover somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like it might signal the hug, but 'hugging' does that; 'around' turns the first word back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Texas is the large southern state of the USA.
